answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The resilience comes from slashing: dishonest approval costs more than the gain from a single manipulated verdict, so rational attackers stay honest. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
